//exclude: The alternate build directories are generated by OTHER instances running from
this same checkout (`dev:qa`, and a build run with NEXT_DIST_DIR set). Their
`dev/types/routes.d.ts` used to be listed in `include`, which made this
typecheck depend on which servers had run — and on one of them not having been
killed mid-write. A half-written copy of that generated file failed the
production build with a syntax error pointing at generated code, and the same
damaged manifest made an existing API route answer a plain 404. The route types
are identical whichever directory produced them, so `.next/types` is enough.
exclude: In `exclude` because a file that is merely IMPORTED by an included one is still
typechecked, so listing `qa` was not enough on its own. `test/studio` reaches into
the Agent Studio, which is a separate program compiled with different options (it
imports with explicit `.ts` extensions, legal only under its own tsconfig). Those
tests are typechecked by `tsconfig.test.json` and the studio by its own config; the
app has no business compiling either.
